image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Triceratops skull fossil mounted on display in an outdoor or museum setting. The skull features the characteristic three horns (two large brow horns, one smaller nasal horn) and a massive solid bony frill. The bone appears weathered and brown. Green foliage and trees are visible in the background, along with a metal support structure holding the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns and a smaller nasal horn. They are structurally intact and correctly positioned.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a fossilized skull. The keratinous beak (rhamphotheca) does not preserve in fossils and is absent from the image. Only the bony premaxilla and dentary are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image contains only the skull and neck/frill assembly. The body and limbs are completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is prominently displayed, extending backward from the skull. Its width appears consistent with Triceratops anatomy, dominating the rear profile of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated). The surface texture is rough due to fossilization but structurally solid. Epoccipitals are visible along the margin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As this is a bare fossil skeleton, no skin, scales, or soft tissue structures are present or visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in the image.
The tail is not visible in the image.
